# EXC 3460 — Worked Diagnostic Cases & Look-Alike Contrast Matrix

> [!info] How to Use This Companion Note
> This file trains **applied OB case diagnosis** across every course unit:
> - **Part 1 (Cases 1–12)**: Twelve flagship multi-concept scenarios walked step-by-step (*Cue Extraction $\to$ Theory Diagnosis $\to$ Distractor Elimination $\to$ Managerial Intervention*).
> - **Part 2 (Master 30-Pair Look-Alike Contrast Matrix)**: Side-by-side tie-breakers for the thirty easiest-to-confuse concept pairs on BI's `A–E` multiple-choice exams.
> - Return to main reference: **[EXC3460 - Organizational Behavior and Leadership](obsidian://open?vault=Obsidian%20Vault&file=EXC3460-Obsidian/EXC3460%20-%20Organizational%20Behavior%20and%20Leadership)** | Practice bank & mock exam: **[Practice](obsidian://open?vault=Obsidian%20Vault&file=EXC3460-Obsidian/EXC3460-support/Practice)**.

## Part 1: Twelve Flagship Diagnostic Case Walkthroughs

### Case 1 — Culture Diagnosis & Iceberg Misalignment (`Lesson 2`)
> [!example] Scenario Prompt
> Nordic MedTech hires brilliant autonomous biotech PhDs by promising *"a culture of bold curiosity like Tesla."* Yet in practice, weekly bonuses punish any failed prototype, engineers follow `80`-page compliance sign-offs without deviation, and open-plan coffee bars sit empty because nobody dares leave their desk before the VP leaves at `18:30`. An HR consultant installs beanbags and a "Fail Fast!" wall poster, yet innovation stays dead. Why?

- **Step 1 — Cue Extraction**: Rhetoric claims **Learning** (*Flexibility + Independent*), yet rewards/rules enforce **Order** (`SEC` rules) and **Safety** (`Lloyd's` caution); physical posters sit *above* the **Culture Iceberg** waterline while unwritten norms & incentives govern *below*.
- **Step 2 — Theory Diagnosis**:
  1. **Culture Iceberg (`Schein / Dawson & Andriopoulos`)**: Beanbags and posters change **surface manifestations** only, leaving **basic assumptions** ("errors kill careers; presenteeism equals loyalty") untouched.
  2. **Groysberg et al. (`2018`) Clash**: Stated **Learning** style (`Tesla`: Flexibility + Independent) contradicts operational **Order/Safety** styles (`Stability + Interdependent`).
  3. **R&J Culture Maintenance (`Lesson 2 Slide 16`)**: Recruitment (*Selection criteria*) sold one identity, while *Top Management actions* and *Socialization* enforced the opposite (**Person–Organization misfit**).
- **Step 3 — Distractor Elimination**: Reject *"weak organizational culture"* — norms here are actually **very strong** (*uniform compliance at desks until 18:30*), just aligned with **Safety/Order** rather than **Learning**!
- **Step 4 — Managerial Intervention**: Pull all **four culture-change levers** simultaneously: senior leaders model leaving early & discussing failed experiments (*Leadership*), rewrite bonuses/promotions to reward smart experimentation (*HR Practices*), cut redundant sign-offs (*Symbols & Structure*), and narrate wins transparently (*Communication*).

---

### Case 2 — Kelley's Attribution Cube & The Pygmalion Spiral (`Lesson 3`)
> [!example] Scenario Prompt
> Nora, a reliable senior account executive (`4` years top quartile), suddenly misses targets across **three straight quarterly reviews** on the newly acquired Nord-West industrial account (*High Consistency*). Yet on her remaining healthcare accounts, Nora continues smashing quotas (`High Distinctiveness`), and **four out of five other reps** assigned to Nord-West industrial accounts also missed targets (`High Consensus`). A new sales director concludes Nora has "lost her work ethic," reassigns her to trivial clerical leads, and stops mentoring her — after which her healthcare metrics plunge too.

- **Step 1 — Cue Extraction**: Distinctiveness = **High** (*only fails on Nord-West*), Consensus = **High** (*peers also fail on Nord-West*), Consistency = **High** (*repeats across 3 quarters*).
- **Step 2 — Theory Diagnosis**:
  1. **Kelley's Attribution Pattern**: `High Distinctiveness + High Consensus + High Consistency` $\implies$ **External Attribution** (*the Nord-West territory/pricing model is structurally broken!*).
  2. **Fundamental Attribution Error (`FAE`)**: The sales director ignored situational evidence (`Consensus`) and blamed internal disposition (*"lost her work ethic"*).
  3. **Golem Effect (`Self-Fulfilling Prophecy`)**: Removing stretch work and coaching communicated low expectations, eroding Nora's confidence and causing performance across her *other* accounts to drop!
- **Step 3 — Distractor Elimination**: Not *Self-Serving Bias* (Nora is not blaming luck for her own ego; the director is judging Nora). Not *Actor–Observer* alone unless contrasting Nora's view vs. director's view.
- **Step 4 — Managerial Intervention**: Audit Nord-West pricing/territory constraints (*External fix*) and restore high-expectation coaching (**Pygmalion**).

---

### Case 3 — Team Dysfunction: Groupthink, Punctuated Equilibrium & Anxiety Zone (`Lesson 4`)
> [!example] Scenario Prompt
> A `10`-week cross-functional launch team spends weeks `1–4` endlessly debating logos and making tiny incremental edits. At the end of **Week `5` (`50%` mark)**, realizing the trade-show deadline looms, they abruptly scrap the old plan and launch frantic coding sprints. However, two junior engineers spot a fatal security bug (`Week 8`), stay silent when the respected CTO declares *"This is our smoothest launch ever — anyone doubting us lacks team spirit!"*, and afterward tell peers privately they knew firing anyone asking "dumb questions" happened last quarter.

- **Step 1 — Cue Extraction**: Temporary `10`-week group with fixed deadline; inertia weeks `1–4` $\to$ abrupt explosion at **Week `5`**; junior silence under enthusiastic boss; fear of humiliation/firing for raising bugs.
- **Step 2 — Theory Diagnosis**:
  1. **Punctuated-Equilibrium Model**: Textbook **Phase 1 inertia $\to$ Midpoint (`50%`) Transition $\to$ Phase 2 sprint** (not smooth Tuckman stages).
  2. **Groupthink (`Janis`)**: Illusion of invulnerability, leader advocacy before dissent, self-censorship, and pressure on dissenters (*"lacks team spirit"*).
  3. **Edmondson's Anxiety Zone**: **High Accountability/Deadlines + Low Psychological Safety** forces error concealment!
- **Step 3 — Distractor Elimination**: Not **Groupshift** (*discussion did not push group to an extreme riskier consensus through open debate — dissent was *silenced* before debate!*). Not **Comfort Zone** (*standards/deadlines are brutal here*).
- **Step 4 — Managerial Intervention**: Leader must speak **last**, appoint a rotating **Devil's Advocate**, and run **Nominal Group Technique (`NGT`)** anonymous risk voting while praising early bug catches (**Learning Zone**).

### Case 4 — Contingency Leadership Matching (`Fiedler`, `Hersey–Blanchard`, `LMX` — `Lesson 5`)
> [!example] Scenario Prompt
> Consider two sub-units inside a shipping logistics firm:
> - **Unit Alpha**: Newly hired warehouse temps who **lack automated scanner skills** AND **feel anxious/reluctant** about the new quota software.
> - **Unit Beta**: A strained crisis task force where the **manager has weak trust with staff (`Poor Relations`)**, the rescue plan is **completely unstructured (`Low Task Structure`)**, and the manager holds **almost zero formal bonus/firing authority (`Low Position Power`)**.

- **Step 1 — Cue Extraction**: Unit Alpha specifies **follower readiness** (`Unable & Unwilling/Insecure`); Unit Beta specifies **situational control** (`Poor relations + Unstructured task + Weak power`).
- **Step 2 — Theory Diagnosis**:
  1. **Unit Alpha (`Hersey–Blanchard SLT`)**: Followers are **`R1` (`Unable & Unwilling/Insecure`)** $\implies$ leader must adapt to **Telling / Directing** (*High Task, Low Relationship*: step-by-step SOPs and clear instructions). Once temps master skills yet remain nervous (`R3`), shift to **Participating**.
  2. **Unit Beta (`Fiedler Contingency`)**: All three control factors are unfavorable $\implies$ **Very Low Situational Control (`Octant VIII`)**. Under Fiedler's inverted U-fit, **Task-Oriented (`Low LPC`)** leadership performs best in **very low** (as well as very high) control!
- **Step 3 — Distractor Elimination**: Do **not** recommend *"tell the Unit Beta leader to flex into high-LPC relationship coaching"* — Fiedler explicitly treats `LPC` style as **fixed** (*either place a Low-LPC leader in charge OR structurally raise task clarity/position power toward Moderate Control!*).

### Case 5 — The Awestruck Trap, Emotional Suppression & Toxic Triangle (`Lesson 6`)
> [!example] Scenario Prompt
> A charismatic biotech CEO delivers electrifying All-Hands speeches framed around moral salvation (*"no child will ever suffer a painful blood draw again"*). Exit surveys after meetings show staff **feel `70%` inspired and clear on corporate strategy**, yet blind pop-quizzes reveal they grasp only **`48%`** of actual operational priorities. Meanwhile, a worried lab lead notices inaccurate assay validation data at `14:00` after the morning keynote, freezes during Q&A with a blank poker face, and tells nobody because devoted mid-level *"believers"* punish skepticism and board audits were dissolved during hyper-growth.

- **Step 1 — Cue Extraction**: High perceived clarity (`70%`) vs. low actual retention (`48%`); afternoon silence after morning charisma; blank faces; compliant believers + absent board governance + crisis hype.
- **Step 2 — Theory Diagnosis**:
  1. **Menges et al. (`2015`) Awestruck Effect**: **Attention narrows $\to$ Self shrinks $\to$ Deference rises**. *"Feeling informed is enough"* explains `70% vs 48%` gap; **"hearts stirred, faces blank"** captures emotional suppression (*"inspire in morning, miss bad news in afternoon"*).
  2. **Padilla, Hogan & Kaiser (`2007`) Toxic Triangle**: Combines a charismatic/Dark-Triad leader + **Susceptible Followers** (*Conformers/Colluders*) + **Conducive Environment** (*dissolved board oversight + hype*).
  3. **Klein & House (`1995`) Charisma on Fire**: Spark (CEO) + Fuel (believing staff) + Oxygen (crisis/urgency).
- **Step 3 — Distractor Elimination**: **Individualized Consideration** (*Transformational leadership's 4th `I`*) would *reverse* this silence by switching into listening mode, not worsen it!

### Case 6 — Attitudes, Emotional Labor & `JD-R` / `EVLN` Diagnosis (`Lesson 7`)
> [!example] Scenario Prompt
> Oslo Customer Support handles frustrated insurance claimants `8 hours/day`. Agents are strictly graded by AI speech monitors to keep an upbeat cheerful tone (**displayed rule**), even when customers scream insults — leaving veteran agents privately furious (`felt anger`). Over `6` months, supervisors notice **role ambiguity** around refund limits and constant **IT system freezes**, alongside high workloads. Agent Maya quietly stops taking overtime, arrives `15` minutes late daily, and leaves claims half-done (`Outcome A`), while Agent Lukas calmly brings an error-log spreadsheet to union/team reps proposing clearer refund authority (`Outcome B`).

- **Step 1 — Cue Extraction**: Faking cheerfulness over felt anger; role ambiguity + red-tape tech freezes; Maya withdraws quietly; Lukas actively proposes constructive fixes.
- **Step 2 — Theory Diagnosis**:
  1. **Emotional Labor (`R&J Ch. 4`)**: Faking outward display = **Surface Acting** $\to$ chronic **emotional dissonance** $\to$ burnout/insomnia (*vs. Deep Acting, which reappraises feelings*).
  2. **Hindrance vs. Challenge Stressors (`R&J Ch. 18`)**: *Role ambiguity* and *system freezes (red tape)* are **Hindrance Stressors** draining energy along the **JD-R Health-Impairment pathway**; scarce refund discretion = low Job Control (**JDCS** high-strain quadrant).
  3. **`EVLN` Contrast**: Maya = **Neglect** (*Passive + Destructive*); Lukas = **Voice** (*Active + Constructive*).
- **Step 3 — Distractor Elimination**: Maya is **not** showing **Exit** (she hasn't resigned/applied out) nor **Loyalty** (Loyalty avoids hurting performance while waiting optimistically).

### Case 7 — Channel Richness, Allen Curve & Change Cooptation (`Lesson 8`)
> [!example] Scenario Prompt
> During a painful restructuring at *Elegance Inc.*, CSO Elena Green emails a `12`-page PDF announcing job relocations across `3` departments with zero town hall Q&A. Within days, productivity plunges on cross-disciplinary R&D projects relocated `45` meters away to a separate wing, and rumors trigger fierce union resistance. To quiet resistance fast, management appoints the loudest union critic to an impressive-sounding *"Future Vision Steering Committee"* whose recommendations management privately plans to ignore.

- **Step 1 — Cue Extraction**: High-ambiguity emotional restructuring delivered via lean text (`Email PDF`); R&D separated by `45 m`; vocal critic given symbolic seat **without real advisory intent**.
- **Step 2 — Theory Diagnosis**:
  1. **Channel Mismatch**: High-ambiguity/high-fear change requires **high-richness face-to-face / synchronous meetings + Active/Reflective listening**, NOT one-way email (`low richness`).
  2. **Allen (`2007`) Distance Decay**: Moving teams `45 m` apart pushes weekly technical interaction below **`0.05`**, starving **Type III (Inspiration)** communication.
  3. **Resistance Tactic (`R&J Ch. 16`)**: Appointing the critic merely for endorsement without genuine input is **Cooptation** (*not true Participation!*), risking total collapse of trust under **Kotter's rule** (*"people follow consistency"*).
- **Step 3 — Distractor Elimination**: Not **Manipulation** strictly in the rumor-twisting sense alone — the classic R&J exact term for *buying off a resistor leader with a symbolic role* is **Cooptation**.

### Case 8 — Deep-Level Diversity & Amabile's Creative Set-Breaking (`Lesson 9`)
> [!example] Scenario Prompt
> A global fintech forms a `6`-person payments team mixing Norwegians, Brazilians, and Japanese specialists across engineering, law, and marketing. In **Week `2`**, misunderstandings over blunt Nordic directness (**Low-Context**) vs. indirect polite hesitation (**High-Context**) trigger tense interpersonal clashes. Rather than shutting the team down, the leader establishes clear project goals, pairs engineers with lawyers over coffee workshops, and connects a cosmetics dispenser designer (*analogical thinking*) to spark a fraud-proof biometric wallet (**both novel AND commercially viable**). By Month `4`, demographic friction fades as members bond over shared analytical curiosity.

- **Step 1 — Cue Extraction**: Early **Surface + National Context** clash; 3 leadership cohesion fixes; cross-industry analogy solving practical + original problem (**Mumford**); Month `4` cohesion built on shared curiosity (**Deep-level**).
- **Step 2 — Theory Diagnosis**:
  1. **Surface vs. Deep Diversity**: Early friction traced to surface cues & **High/Low Context communication**, bridged into **Deep-level value fit** (*"Us vs Them" $\to$ "We"*, task-focused leader, intergroup contact).
  2. **Mumford (`2003`) & Amabile (`1983`)**: Product shows **Novelty + Usefulness** (**Creativity**), driven by **Creativity-Relevant Processes** (*set-breaking via analogical association*), **Domain Skills**, and **Intrinsic Motivation** — following **Wallas (`1926`)** (*Preparation $\to$ Incubation $\to$ Illumination $\to$ Verification*).

### Case 9 — Scaling `NordTech` & Perrow `2×2` Structural Fit (`Lesson 10`)
> [!example] Scenario Prompt
> *NordTech* grew from `40` friends in a co-working loft to `600` employees across Oslo, Munich, and Austin. Meanwhile, within its operations, **Unit 1 (`Customer Billing Processing`)** executes predictable invoice checks via standardized rules (*low exceptions, clear manualized steps*), whereas **Unit 2 (`Next-Gen Quantum Encryption R&D`)** tackles unpredictable breakthroughs with no existing textbook (`high exceptions, unanalyzable problems`). Also, management introduces `45`-minute structured behavioral interviews + work-sample coding tasks for all `600`-scale hires.

- **Step 1 — Cue Extraction**: Rapid size jump (`40 -> 600` breaks Simple structure); two units differ sharply on **Perrow's Task Variability × Problem Analyzability**; HR upgrades from unstructured chats to structured + work samples.
- **Step 2 — Theory Diagnosis**:
  1. **Size & Structure**: At `40`, **Simple Structure** thrived; at `600`, founder central bottleneck fails $\to$ shift to **divisional/hybrid design** (*keeping **Mechanistic** controls in Unit 1 Billing and **Organic Team** subunits in Unit 2 R&D!*).
  2. **Perrow's `2×2` (`Sample Exam Q10`)**: Unit 1 = **Routine** (*low variability + analyzable*) $\to$ **Mechanistic**; Unit 2 = **Nonroutine** (*high variability + unanalyzable*) $\to$ **Organic** (*Note: R&D scientists still have **high work specialization** alongside **low formalization**!*).
  3. **HR Selection (`R&J Ch. 17`)**: Pairing **Work Samples** (*substantive performance-simulation*) + **Structured Interviews** maximizes predictive validity and cuts contrast/halo bias.

### Case 10 — Algorithmic Control Paradoxes (`Lesson 11` & `Tech Q1–Q4`)
> [!example] Scenario Prompt
> Compare two gig/knowledge workplaces:
> - **Firm X (Management Consultancy)**: Gives consultants top-tier iPhones with "zero mandatory evening check-in policy." Soon, ambitious analysts reply at `23:30` to signal commitment; within months, partners expect instant evening responses and burnout spikes.
> - **Platform Y (Freelance Coding Marketplace)**: Evaluates coders using a proprietary *"Reliability Index"* whose exact weighting formula changes secretly every few weeks. Workers terrified of sudden ranking drops accept unpaid revisions and work rigidly off-peak shifts, yet never organize strikes because pop-up banners call tweaks *"Experimental Quality Safeguards Protecting Fair Freelancers."*

- **Step 1 — Cue Extraction**: Firm X = voluntary mobile adoption $\to$ escalated norm $\to$ trapped availability; Platform Y = opaque dynamic rating (`6 R's` *Rating/Recording*) + anxiety-driven self-restraint + benign rhetorical framing.
- **Step 2 — Theory Diagnosis**:
  1. **Firm X = Mazmanian, Orlikowski & Yates (`2013`) Autonomy Paradox** (*plus R&J `p. 615` proof that unchecked late-night smartphone usage destroys recovery!*).
  2. **Platform Y = Rahman (`2021`) *The Invisible Cage*** (opaque scoring breeds self-constraining compliance) + **Rahman, Weiss & Karunakaran (`2024`) *The Pacifying Algorithm*** (experimental framing neutralizes collective resistance) operating atop **Kellogg et al.'s (`2020`) `6 R's`**.

### Case 11 — JCM `MPS` Numerical Audit, Vroom Zero-Veto & Four Justice Dimensions (`Lesson 12`)
> [!example] Scenario Prompt
> A medical claims analyst role currently scores (`1–7` scale): `Skill Variety = 5`, `Task Identity = 2`, `Task Significance = 8`... wait: suppose standard `1–7` JCM ratings are `Skill Variety = 5`, `Task Identity = 2`, `Task Significance = 5`, **`Autonomy = 1`**, `Feedback = 4`. Management proposes two plans:
> - **Plan A (Horizontal)**: Add two more repetitive data-entry forms (`Task Identity` rises to `5`, keeping `Autonomy = 1`).
> - **Plan B (Vertical)**: Give analysts end-to-end client ownership, schedule discretion (`Autonomy = 5`), and direct client satisfaction scorecards (`Feedback = 6`), **without** changing `(5, 2, 5)`.
> Separately, when cutting year-end bonuses, Manager K applies transparent metrics evenly (`Procedural`), yet snaps *"Be grateful you still have a job!"* (`?`) and gives zero explanation why thresholds shifted (`?`). Furthermore, Manager K offers a `\$5,000` bonus tied to hitting an impossible quota that workers know nobody has ever met (`E = 0`).

- **Step 1 — Numerical JCM Calculation**:
  $$\text{Baseline MPS} = \frac{5 + 2 + 5}{3} \times 1 \times 4 = 4 \times 1 \times 4 = \mathbf{16}$$
  - **Under Plan A (*Job Enlargement*)**:
    $$\text{MPS}_A = \frac{5 + 5 + 5}{3} \times 1 \times 4 = 5 \times 1 \times 4 = \mathbf{20} \quad (\text{tiny } +25\% \text{ gain!})$$
  - **Under Plan B (*Job Enrichment*)**:
    $$\text{MPS}_B = \frac{5 + 2 + 5}{3} \times 5 \times 6 = 4 \times 5 \times 6 = \mathbf{120} \quad (\mathbf{7.5\times \text{ higher MPS}}!)$$
- **Step 2 — Theory Diagnosis**:
  1. **Job Enrichment (`Plan B`) beats Job Enlargement (`Plan A`)** massively because `Autonomy` and `Feedback` act as **multipliers** in `MPS`!
  2. **Vroom Expectancy Zero-Veto**: Even with huge `Valence` (`\$5,000`), an impossible quota drives **`Expectancy` ($E \to 0$)**, making $\text{Motivation} = 0 \times I \times V = \mathbf{0}$.
  3. **Four-Way Justice (`Slide 51`)**: *Procedural Justice* held (transparent metric), yet **Interpersonal Injustice** (rude humiliation) and **Informational Injustice** (withheld reasoning) trigger retaliation!

### Case 12 — Sunk Costs (`NOK 500k`), Bounded Rationality & Spotify Integrative Bargaining (`Lessons 13–14`)
> [!example] Scenario Prompt
> *(Part A)* A SaaS founder spent `6` months and **`NOK 500,000`** building a student timetable app that `92%` of beta testers abandoned within `3` days. With **`NOK 100,000`** and `1` month of runway left, her mentor advises pivoting immediately to B2B university scheduling, while her co-founder argues: *"If we pivot now, the `NOK 500,000` was all for nothing — let's spend our last `NOK 100,000` on ads!"*
> *(Part B)* Meanwhile, an indie artist negotiates with **Spotify**: Spotify starts at a **`€200,000` advance**, artist demands **`€500,000`**. Artist actually values algorithmic/editorial playlist exposure and owning masters after `2` years far more than instant upfront cash, while Spotify needs exclusive streaming window guarantees for `2027` but cares little about giving extra algorithmic onboarding support. Artist also holds a signed backup offer (`€260,000` value) from Apple Music (**BATNA**).

- **Step 1 — Cue Extraction**: Non-recoverable `NOK 500,000` driving desperate double-down on failing app; multi-issue Spotify deal where parties weigh cash vs. playlist push vs. exclusivity differently + Apple backup.
- **Step 2 — Theory Diagnosis**:
  1. **Part A — Escalation of Commitment / Sunk Cost Fallacy** (*matching **Concorde** & Lesson 13 Slide 35 case!*): Past `NOK 500,000` is gone regardless; rational choice evaluates *only* expected future return on the remaining `NOK 100,000`. Note also the **Learning Formula**: `Experience + Feedback (92% churn) + Reflection + Change`!
  2. **Part B — Distributive $\to$ Integrative Bargaining + BATNA**: Haggling only over `€200k` vs. `€500k` creates fixed-pie **Distributive** gridlock (*note Spotify must beat the artist's **`€260k` Apple Music BATNA** or artist walks!*). Trading **moderate cash (`~€280k`) + heavy playlist placement + `18-month` exclusivity** exploits asymmetric priorities to **expand the pie (`Integrative Win–Win`)**!

| :-: | :--- | :--- | :--- | :-: |

| **3** | **Surface Culture** *(Iceberg tip)* | **Deep Basic Assumptions** | Visible logos/offices/dress codes vs. **unspoken mental schemes, status norms & "how we do things"** | [§2.3](obsidian://open?vault=Obsidian%20Vault&file=EXC3460-Obsidian/EXC3460%20-%20Organizational%20Behavior%20and%20Leadership%232.3%20The%20Culture%20Iceberg%2C%20Workspaces%2C%20Ceremonies%20%26%20Tall%20vs.%20Flat%20Hierarchies) |
| **4** | **Dominant Culture** | **Subculture / Counterculture** | Core values shared by majority vs. unit-specific extra norms (**Subculture**) or opposing values (**Counter**) | [§2.4](obsidian://open?vault=Obsidian%20Vault&file=EXC3460-Obsidian/EXC3460%20-%20Organizational%20Behavior%20and%20Leadership%232.4%20Subcultures%2C%20Countercultures%2C%20and%20Professional%20Cultures) |

| **9** | **Tuckman `5` Stages** | **Punctuated Equilibrium** | Ongoing general groups (*Forming–Adjourning*) vs. **temporary deadline groups jumping at the exact 50% midpoint** | [§4.2](obsidian://open?vault=Obsidian%20Vault&file=EXC3460-Obsidian/EXC3460%20-%20Organizational%20Behavior%20and%20Leadership%234.2%20Group%20Development%3A%20Tuckman%20vs.%20Punctuated%20Equilibrium) |
